facts.heading: Exhausted since October
facts.content: Daniel has been completely burned out since October. He works as a project manager at a logistics company.
facts.evidence: I've been completely burned out since October.

facts.heading: Work workload increased
facts.content: Daniel ended up doing three people's jobs after losing a big client.
facts.evidence: I ended up doing three people's jobs.

facts.heading: Work bleeds into personal time
facts.content: Daniel answers messages at night and thinks about work even when not working.
facts.evidence: I'm at my desk by seven and I'm still answering messages at ten at night. Even when I'm not working I'm thinking about work.

facts.heading: Poor sleep quality
facts.content: Daniel's sleep is terrible, and he sleeps about four hours most nights.
facts.evidence: Most nights I sleep about four hours.

facts.heading: Wakes up at three AM
facts.content: Daniel wakes up at three in the morning and cannot fall back asleep.
facts.evidence: I wake up at three in the morning and can't fall back asleep.

facts.heading: Waking thoughts are work related
facts.content: When Daniel wakes up, his thoughts focus on shipping schedules, the client, or forgotten details.
facts.evidence: My head just starts. Shipping schedules, the client, whether I've forgotten something.

facts.heading: Dreading the nights
facts.content: Daniel has started dreading the nights because of the sleep pattern.
facts.evidence: I've started dreading the nights, if I'm honest.

facts.heading: Father diagnosed with Parkinson's
facts.content: Daniel's father was diagnosed with Parkinson's disease in the autumn.
facts.evidence: My father. He was diagnosed with Parkinson's disease in the autumn.

facts.heading: Father's current condition
facts.content: Daniel's father's hands shake, he is slower, and he gets frustrated.
facts.evidence: His hands shake, and he's slower, and he gets frustrated.

facts.heading: Daniel drives father
facts.content: Daniel is the one who drives his father to the hospital in Leeds.
facts.evidence: I'm the one who drives him to the hospital in Leeds.

facts.heading: Care responsibility is singular
facts.content: Daniel is solely responsible for his father's care as his sister lives in Toronto.
facts.evidence: all the care for our father falls on me.

facts.heading: Guilt about being tired
facts.content: Daniel feels guilty for being tired when his father is ill.
facts.evidence: I feel it's selfish to be tired when he's the one who's ill.

facts.heading: Avoids sharing feelings
facts.content: Daniel does not tell anyone about his feelings regarding his exhaustion.
facts.evidence: So I don't say anything to anyone.

facts.heading: Sister does not help
facts.content: Daniel's younger sister Hannah lives in Toronto and cannot provide care.
facts.evidence: She calls him every Sunday, and she's not the one who's neglecting him.

facts.heading: Hides true feelings
facts.content: Daniel tells his sister he is fine when asked how he is.
facts.evidence: She asks how I am and I say fine.

facts.heading: Wants to express distress
facts.content: Daniel wishes his sister would know that he is not fine.
facts.evidence: That I'm not fine.

facts.heading: GP visit results
facts.content: Daniel had blood tests that were all normal. The GP said it is stress and exhaustion.
facts.evidence: She did blood tests, and they were all normal. She said it's stress and exhaustion

facts.heading: Refused to talk to GP
facts.content: Daniel told his GP he had no time to talk about his stress and exhaustion.
facts.evidence: I said I hadn't got time.

facts.heading: Girlfriend booked therapy
facts.content: Daniel's girlfriend Claire booked a session for him. Claire said she was done watching him disappear.
facts.evidence: My girlfriend booked it, to be honest. Claire. She said she was done watching me disappear.

facts.heading: Claire is patient
facts.content: Claire is patient and makes Daniel tea without pushing him to talk. Claire is also starting to feel the effects.
facts.evidence: She's very patient. She makes me tea and doesn't push me to talk. But I can see it's wearing on her too.

facts.heading: Stopped running activity
facts.content: Daniel stopped running ten kilometres every Saturday morning about two months ago. He stopped because his legs felt like lead.
facts.evidence: I stopped about two months ago. My legs felt like lead, and then I just never went back.

facts.heading: Lost part of self
facts.content: Daniel feels like he has lost a part of himself since stopping running. He felt running was the one time a week nobody could reach him.
facts.evidence: Like I've lost a part of myself. It was the one time in the week nobody could reach me.

facts.heading: Difficulty saying yes
facts.content: Daniel avoids saying yes to social invitations because of work emails and potential needs from his Dad.
facts.evidence: The emails. If I'm away I'll come back to two hundred of them. And Dad might need something.

facts.heading: No time for rest
facts.content: Daniel cannot remember the last time he was properly off. He feels that rest has a price.
facts.evidence: I can't remember the last time I was properly off.

facts.heading: Boss sends late emails
facts.content: Daniel's boss Peterson sends emails at eleven at night and expects an answer before breakfast.
facts.evidence: He sends emails at eleven at night and expects an answer before breakfast.

facts.heading: Answers emails constantly
facts.content: Daniel answers every email from his boss, even when he is in bed. Claire dislikes this behavior.
facts.evidence: I answer it. Every time. Even if I'm in bed. Claire hates it.

facts.heading: Fear of job loss
facts.content: Daniel is afraid his boss might think he is not committed due to a restructuring in the spring.
facts.evidence: That he'd think I wasn't committed. There's a restructuring in the spring and I'm afraid they'll let me go.

facts.heading: Ambivalence about job loss
facts.content: Daniel thinks he might feel relieved if he is let go, but also horrible about being relieved because he has a mortgage.
facts.evidence: I think part of me would be relieved, and then I'd feel horrible about being relieved. I have a mortgage.

facts.heading: Mood is flat and irritable
facts.content: Daniel's moods apart from tiredness are flat and irritable. He snapped at a colleague last week over nothing.
facts.evidence: Flat, mostly. And irritable. I snapped at a colleague last week over nothing

facts.heading: Panic attack symptoms
facts.content: When Daniel snapped at a colleague, his heart was going and his hands were shaking. He briefly thought it was a heart attack.
facts.evidence: My heart was going and my hands were shaking. I thought for a second it was a heart attack, but it passed.

facts.heading: Frightening event on train
facts.content: Daniel had to get off and stand on the platform. This has happened a couple of times.
facts.evidence: Once on the train to Manchester. I just had to get off and stand on the platform.

facts.heading: Fear of losing control
facts.content: Daniel is afraid that he is losing it. He fears he will not be coping.
facts.evidence: That I'm losing it. That I'm going to end up like, I don't know. Not coping.

facts.heading: Coffee consumption habit
facts.content: Daniel drinks about six cups of coffee a day.
facts.evidence: I'm on about six cups a day.

facts.heading: Evening wine consumption
facts.content: Daniel has started having wine in the evenings to switch his head off. He drinks two to three glasses.
facts.evidence: And I've started having wine in the evenings to switch my head off. Two glasses, sometimes three.

facts.heading: Wine effect on sleep
facts.content: Daniel finds the wine uneasy and notes it does not help him sleep.
facts.evidence: Uneasy. It works for an hour and then I wake at three anyway. I know it's not helping.

facts.heading: Feeling about self-disclosure
facts.content: Daniel felt a bit of a relief after speaking about his feelings.
facts.evidence: Strange. A bit of a relief, actually. Like putting down a bag I didn't realise I was carrying.

facts.heading: Desire to sleep
facts.content: Daniel thinks that if he could sleep, he could probably cope with the rest.
facts.evidence: The nights, I think. If I could sleep I could probably cope with the rest.

facts.heading: Family influence on coping
facts.content: Daniel's grandfather never complained about anything. His father also does not complain.
facts.evidence: My grandfather worked in the mines in Yorkshire. He never complained about anything, not once. Dad's the same. You just get on with it.

facts.heading: Belief about being weak
facts.content: Daniel thinks his grandfather would think he was weak for being there.
facts.evidence: I keep thinking he would think I was weak for being here.

facts.heading: Self-talk about self
facts.content: Daniel wants to tell his grandfather he is not weak but very tired.
facts.evidence: That I'm not weak. I'm just very tired.

facts.heading: Belief about self-talk
facts.content: Daniel is unsure if he believes he can say this to himself.
facts.evidence: Maybe. I don't know if I believe it yet.

facts.heading: Proposed coping strategy
facts.content: Daniel is willing to try a small change to his routine.
facts.evidence: Yes. Half past nine, perhaps. I could make it a thing with Claire. Tea on the sofa.

facts.heading: Agreed to meet next week
facts.content: Daniel agreed to meet again next week. He mentioned the trains are awful.
facts.evidence: Same time next week? Yes. I'll be here. I'll try to make it on time, the trains are awful.
